messages:
acme-cso: Hi, after rotating our KMS key yesterday some of our uploads started failing when Redwood calls Decrypt. We get InvalidCiphertextException from your service. No code changes on our side except key rotation.

raj (support): Thanks — can you paste the exact error/log and a sample ciphertext (base64)? Also confirm whether you changed the CMK or enabled rotation on the same key.

acme-cso: Logs:
```
2026-03-11T09:02:10Z ERROR decrypt failed: InvalidCiphertextException: The ciphertext refers to a key that does not exist in this account.
requestId=xyz-789
ciphertext=...AQICAH...==
```
We created a new CMK and updated alias acme-rw to point to it. We also accidentally changed an encryption-context key from \"env\":\"prod\" -> \"env\":\"prod-1\" in a terraform PR for one service.

anne (eng-security): Two likely causes: 1) if you replaced the CMK (new key-id) old ciphertexts can't be decrypted via the alias; 2) encryption-context mismatch is case-sensitive and must match exactly. Can you provide CloudTrail Encrypt events and the exact encryption-context used when encrypting?

miguel (customer-ops): CloudTrail shows Encrypt calls using arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222:key/old-key-id at 2026-03-10T12:30Z. Alias update (UpdateAlias) to arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222:key/new-key-id at 2026-03-11T07:15Z. We ran a local decrypt against old-key-id with the original ctx and it succeeded.

sara (infra): That aligns: once alias points to a new key, Decrypt calls that use the alias will route to the new key. If our service calls Decrypt with alias rather than the original key-id, it will fail for ciphertexts created under the old key. We should check what our SDK sends: alias ARN vs explicit key-id.

oliver (eng-ml): Repro locally:
```
# generate cipher under alias->old-key
aws kms generate-data-key --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222:alias/acme-rw --encryption-context '{"service":"redwood","tenant":"acme","env":"prod"}' --query CiphertextBlob --output text | base64 --decode > sample.ct

# update alias to point to new-key
# then decrypt via alias -> fails
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://sample.ct --encryption-context '{"service":"redwood","tenant":"acme","env":"prod"}'
# InvalidCiphertextException

# decrypt using old-key-id and same ctx -> succeeds
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://sample.ct --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222:key/old-key-id --encryption-context '{"service":"redwood","tenant":"acme","env":"prod"}'
```

anne (eng-security): Support checklist to send to customer:
- exact key ARNs for Encrypt events and current alias mapping
- exact encryption-context map (JSON) used at Encrypt time
- sample ciphertext + timestamp
- confirm whether old CMK was scheduled for deletion or removed

raj (support): Proposed mitigation options:
- customer re-point alias back to old-key-id temporarily so we can drain and re-encrypt
- customer re-encrypt affected data with new CMK
- short-term: customer provide the original key-id in metadata so our service can try Decrypt with that first

miguel (customer-ops): Customer can re-point alias for a 20 minute window. They will also revert the terraform change to ctx. They granted us a short-lived cross-account decrypt grant for investigation.

sara (infra): Internal actions:
- verify our KMS calls use alias vs stored key-id (INF-5423)
- add a logging marker to record key-id used for GenerateDataKey so we can persist it with the ciphertext metadata
- update runbook to check CloudTrail for UpdateAlias between Encrypt and Decrypt timestamps

anne (eng-security): Recommend we also modify SDK behavior: if uploader supplies x-kms-key-id header, persist and use it at Decrypt time as a primary key identifier. Also add clear docs about encryption-context exactness.

raj (support): I'll coordinate with the customer during the alias window. Thanks everyone — I'll update ticket INF-5423 when resolved.
